title: Expected Edge Agreement Under Candidate Decoding
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with label set $\text{Fin}(q)$, choose a candidate subset of labels for each vertex, and fix a default label. Independently at each vertex, choose a label uniformly from its candidate subset when that subset is nonempty, and choose the default otherwise. For any vertex $v$ and neighbor $w$ of $v$, the expected indicator that the game's permutation on $(v,w)$ sends the label at $w$ to the label at $v$ equals the nested candidate average of that same agreement indicator, with the default used for an empty candidate subset.
